text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Talks are underway between the United States and Macedonia on possible leasing of military training ground Krivolak in exchange for military equipment. The U.S. military attache in Skopje denies any knowledge of those arrangements.

- The new Macedonian government held its first session on Monday. The Prime Minister appointed deputy prime ministers - Zlatka Popovska (Socialist Party), Dimitar Buslevski (Social Democratic Alliance) and Naser Ziberi (Party For Democratic Prosperity).
- Participation of Albanian ambassador to Macedonia Shaban Murati in the work of ethnic Albanian parties in Macedonia is interpreted as interference in Macedonia's internal affairs, paper commentary.

- The government's development programme envisages a cut in spending for social services which will provoke discontent. Employees in the public sector announce new strikes while pensioners fear new government retirement plans.
- Largest opposition party VMRO DPMNE starts talks with the parliamentary opposition Liberal Democratic Party for a joint stance on early elections.
- Mayor of Gostivar Rufi Osmani stands firm on his stand that the Albanian flag should remain in front of the Gostivar municipality. He refuses to implement the ruling of the Constitutional Court.
